Subject: ACME - RAG eval follow-up & retriever/reranker recommendations

Thanks again for the time today  great discussion. Below is a concise post-call recap, our recommended evaluation plan, and the concrete next steps we propose for a short POC.

Recap / priorities you shared:
- Primary goal: improve grounding for answers coming from internal KB (policy + product docs) while keeping latency and cost under control.
- SLA target for POC: p50 generation latency <= 250ms, p95 < 900ms.
- Budget constraint: prefer configurations that reduce per-query token cost by ~30% vs heavy-cross-encoder-only approaches.

High-level recommendation (short):
1) Retriever: dense vector retriever using redwood/sim-384 embeddings + FAISS index (or Pinecone if you prefer managed). Chunking: ~500-token chunks with 50-token overlap; keep canonical doc metadata for source attribution.
2) Two-stage rerank: bi-encoder shortlist (k=50) -> cross-encoder rerank top 10. This balances recall and precision while limiting cross-encoder calls.
3) Reranker candidate: redwood/rerank-cross-small for production (good precision/latency tradeoff). As an experiment we can also try a larger cross model (redwood/rerank-cross-large) for quality baseline.
4) Generation: start with redwood/ori-7b-quant for cost-sensitive baseline, and redwood/ori-13b for a quality baseline. We can include a 70B-like variant for headroom if needed.

Evaluation & metrics we propose to measure during the POC:
- Grounding accuracy: % of responses with a correct source (manual review + auto heuristics).
- Retrieval recall @1/@5 and MRR on the labeled eval set.
- Hallucination rate: fraction of answers with unsupported assertions (manual sample).
- Precision@k for reranker.
- Latency distributions (p50/p95) and cost per query.

Artifacts attached / shared:
- acme_prompt_set_v2.csv (prompt set / eval questions you approved on the call)
- acme_benchmark_results_q1.xlsx (current baseline we ran against your exported KB)
- reranker_proposal.pdf (short doc comparing the two-stage approach vs single-stage cross-only)
- Shared drive: https://redwood.app/drive/ACME-RAG-eval (has dashboards & eval harness)

Recommended next steps (proposal):
1) Agree on two configs to A/B for 72 hours:
   - Config A (cost baseline): ori-7b-quant + dense retriever + bi-encoder shortlisting + small cross-encoder rerank on top10.
   - Config B (quality baseline): ori-13b + same retriever + larger cross-encoder reranker.
2) Run automated evals on your prompt set (we'll run retrieval-only metrics + generate 500 responses for manual review sample).
3) Shared dashboard & weekly sync 30-min to review grounding and regressions.

Ask: Can we get approval to run the 72-hour A/B POC on a snapshot of your KB this week? If yes, we'll schedule the work and send a short MA (mutual action) plan with milestones.

Thanks  happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the config tradeoffs.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Sarah  quick answers from an infra/engineering POV: 
- Grounding threshold: 85% is an aggressive but reasonable target for a cleaned KB with canonical sources; for noisy or partially-structured docs we typically see 70-80% without reranker, and 85-92% after a cross-encoder rerank on top10.
- Manual review sample: we recommend 250 responses per config as a pragmatic sample; if you want more statistical power we can scale to 500 but that will add reviewer time. So 250/config is our default.
- Indexing: FAISS is not strictly required. We can push dense vectors into your Elasticsearch cluster (dense_vector fields) for the POC. Performance might differ vs FAISS; we'll include an index-level baseline run. If you prefer no infra changes, we can run retrieval from a temporary FAISS index hosted in our Dedicated test pool and only exchange vector exports (read-only).
- Data access: we only need a snapshot export of the subset you approved (S3 link preferred or secure Drive). We will not keep copies beyond the POC window; we can sign an addendum if needed.

I'll attach a short reranker_proposal.pdf with the perf/cost estimates and a rough job runtime: full retrieval + rerank evaluation on your 12k-chunk snapshot should run ~4-8 hours depending on instance sizing.

I'll kick off a micro-run as soon as Marissa confirms configs  happy to coordinate the infra side.

Thanks,
